## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

HomeViewModel — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/home/HomeViewModel.kt

## Trigger

The home screen, shown at every app launch and whenever the user
returns to it — it is the watch's entry screen.

## Today

`HomeViewModel` combines `RaceRepository.observeReference()`,
`ProfileRepository.observe()` and `RecordedRaceSyncService.observe()`
into `HomeUiState`, and only calls
`ConnectivityPermissionManager.onLaunch()` once in `init`. It never
references `SensorPermissionManager`. `HomeUiState` carries
`referenceLineText`, `referenceTotalTime`, `hasReference`,
`startLabel`, `historyLabel`, `syncLabel` and `syncState`, with no
field for a sensor-access reminder. `SensorPermissionManager` exists
(`app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/sensor/permission/SensorPermissionManager.kt`),
exposing `onLaunch()` and `requestAgain()` — the latter reopens the
system prompt when `SensorPermissionSystem.canShowSystemPrompt()` is
true, or calls `system.openAppSettings()` otherwise — but only
`SensorPermissionViewModel` / `SensorPermissionScreen` call it, on
their own separate screen; nothing routes from the home page to it.

## Expected

The home screen shows a reminder when sensor access is not granted,
and an action that lets the user re-request it — calling
`SensorPermissionManager.requestAgain()`, which reopens the system
prompt when still offered or opens the app's settings page otherwise.
`HomeUiState` carries the state needed to render that reminder and
`HomeViewModel` reads `SensorPermissionManager`'s current state and
exposes an action that calls `requestAgain()`.
